r0079: 40.  The applicant alleged that he had sustained pecuniary damage corresponding to the loss of earnings over the twenty years he would have to spend in prison, which he assessed at 53,280,000,000 Turkish liras (EUR 35,520). He further claimed to have sustained non-pecuniary damage in the amount of 50,000,000,000 Turkish liras (EUR 33,333) on account of his conviction, in particular on the basis of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (*loi sur le terrorisme*).
r0080: 41.  The Government considered the amounts claimed by the applicant to be excessive and unjustified. In that connection, they submitted, as regards pecuniary damage, that there was no causal link between the violation and the loss of earnings alleged by the applicant. As regards non-pecuniary damage, the Government considered that the finding of a violation constituted sufficient just satisfaction.
r0081: 42.  As regards the alleged pecuniary damage, the Court cannot speculate as to what the outcome of the proceedings before the National Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l’Etat*) would have been had the breach of the Convention not occurred. There is therefore no reason to award the applicant compensation for pecuniary damage (see Findlay v. the United Kingdom, judgment of 25 February 1997, Reports of Judgments and Decisions 1997-I, p. 284, § 85).
r0082: 43.  As regards compensation for non-pecuniary damage, the Court considers that, in the circumstances of the case, the finding of a violation constitutes in itself sufficient just satisfaction for the non-pecuniary damage alleged (see Çıraklar, cited above, p. 3074, § 49).
r0084: 44.  The applicant claimed a total of EUR 4,226, supported by vouchers, for the costs and expenses relating to his representation. That sum included the costs of the domestic proceedings and of the proceedings before the Convention institutions.
r0085: 45.  The Government submitted that the documents produced by the applicant did not substantiate the amount claimed.
r0086: 46.  On the basis of the information in its possession, the Court, ruling on an equitable basis, awards the applicant EUR 3,000, less the EUR 630 paid by the Council of Europe by way of legal aid which have not already been taken into account in the claim.
r0088: 47.  The Court considers it appropriate that the default interest should be based on the marginal lending rate of the European Central Bank, to which should be added three percentage points.
